Create "Small bug fixes and tweaks" plan in docs/plans/p102_small-bug-fixes-and-tweaks.md

Category: Bug, Refactor

Fix or tweak these list items:
- When loading the page the browser console warns: "using deprecated parameters for the initialization function; pass a single object instead". There is an issue for this but it seems to be closed/solved: https://github.com/dimforge/rapier/issues/811 . Maybe updating Rapier could help.
- For some reason either changing to or having it as the debug start scene, the Space demo scene console warns (twice) about having multiple instance of Three.js being imported: "THREE.WARNING: Multiple instances of Three.js being imported." (x2).
- If a custom domain Spatial index has wirefame set on and we change a scene the console warns: Calling [RenderPassEncoder (unlabeled)].Draw with a vertex count of 0 is unusual. This should be fixed (probably is trying to draw lines for something that isn't there).
- When the master loop is turned of (from the on-screen tools or from the Loop controls debugger drawer tab), disable the debug camera transforms. What happens is that panning/dragging is still recorded on the screen even if the master loop is not on. After the master loop is toggled on, all the transforms made are actualized by the debug camera moving to a new position.
- Make the Top-down test scene's and the GYM (3rd person) scene's key input's be in the scene scope. Now when I open the App key shortcuts dialog, it lists them under the All scenes list. In the Gym scene there is also the phyisc stress test. That should be scene scoped as well. Then in the ECS test scene there are the ECS stress test keys (two keys) and those should be scoped to the scene as well.
- The on-screen tools' left top corner groups should have equal spacing. Now the AE symbol (about button) and the undo/redo buttons are in the same group but the view switchers are in a separate group. They should be in the same group.

If any of these fixes/tweaks are large refactorings/fixes then produce a separate plan for each large one.

If for some reason this plan or some of its features can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

Create "Fog system" plan in docs/plans/p102_fog-system.md

Category: Fog

Create a fog system for Aekasha. The debugger drawer should have its own  Fog system tab (design an icon for this) and each fog setup should be scene specific. It should be toggleable on/off (the whole system) and it should have at least three different fog passes available to choose from (or notify if some of these should not be implemented, or something else would be beneficial for Aekasha):
- Basic Three.js fog (simple fog)
- Three.js FogExp2
- Global volumetric fog (or something like it)
Also all the parameters for the fog should be editable in the debugger drawer. It can be defined in its own file: myScene.fog.json.

Context from the removed sky box plans (p110-p115; full texts in git history): fog coupling with the sky box was an explicit non-goal of the sky box epic, so it is open for this plan. The sky box's `ground` layer already has `useAtmosphereHorizon` (blends toward the atmosphere's horizon colour, a form of aerial perspective), and the day-night cycle changes the horizon colour over time, so consider a fog colour that can follow the active sky box. Screen-space passes belong in the PostFX chain (`core/PostFX.ts`). Headless WebGPU doesn't render under WSL2, so visual checks need a real browser.

If for some reason this plan or some of its features can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
Create "Billboard text and decal text features" plan set, from priority 390 onwards.

Category: Text

We should be able to add billboard text entities to the world (or attach them to the other entities). If they shouldn't be entities, then give a reason why not and suggest an alternative. I did some research and was quite interested in the SDF/MSDF text method but did not fully understand it. Study the different possibilities considering performance and text quality/sharpness. I would like to have the text symbols be able to (if not all then some) have these features:
- world-space text
- UI text
- labels
- debug overlays
- distance fields
- outlines
- color pulse
- glow
- drop shadows
- blur
- world space sizing or fixed sizing options
- option to have it as a billboard or have it have regular world plane orientation
- fade in/fade out as the text is added to or removed from a world/scene
(these features should not affect performance if turned off)

If we need to somehow import different fonts, we should be have a helper to transform fonts into Aekasha fonts and this could be a command line tool with a package.json script which defines the font which we want to import. If it is not needed, then describe the font formats that can be used. If the fonts are too large of a set (sometimes we only need for example numbers), then research the possibility to only select certain characters from a font. Could this be a build optimization to include only characters that are used (if opted in, because this would not work for all cases such as dynamic text, player names etc.)? I am not sure if this how modern engines build these nowadays, but if I am way of, please suggest something else.

We should also be able to add text decals to meshes. I am not sure if this requires a separate material or a custom node we can attach to any TSL material, but we should be able to add text to meshes with positioning and orientation, and if possible also be able to add some effects to the text (such as worn out text). If it would act the same way as adding any decals to a mesh then the whole decal system should be added as a plan here as well.

Debugger wise the decals should be editable from the material editor. There is a plan for the material editor view so these decal feature(s) should be blocked by that. In the material editor we should be able to attach decals, edit the text (if text decal), select the placement, select color, FX, what else? What about normal and other maps for the text, can they be implemented (maybe not as maps but normal map as a value that would make the text look like thick paint or something like that if possible)? I don't yet have the saving feature (I need a backend to handle saving files), but I would love to have the option to bake the decal onto the material if possible, so keep that in mind for future implementations.

If for some reason this plan or some of its features or some features of it can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

Create "Refactor dynamic character code" plan in docs/plans/p070_refactor-dynamic-character-code.md

Category: Character

UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
The dynamic character sensors are currently failing for some cases. For example the wall glide does not work if the character jumps on a ledge, it gets stuck (for example the side of the stairs when the character is a bit over a part of the stairs but not completely and it also happens for a thin ledge or moving platform). Also the slope detection fails and I am able to jump up a slope that should be impossible. This needs fixing as well. Then when the character jumps over an object that it should clear by jumping, one of the sensors causes a small nudge or sometimes just stops the player from moving in the direction it is headed. Fix this. Also the overall code should be more readable and developer friendly (not sure if this has already been done, but check please).

We should also add/change some of the features:
- For the character that moves to the direction pressed on the keyboard (pressing left arrow or A moves the player left/west, pressing up arrow or W moves the player up/north, etc.) we need to add a property for rotating the character fully to the direction it was heading. Currently if we move the player only a little to the opposite direction it was headed, the rotation stops at the moment the movement key is lifted. If this new property would be turned on, the character would continue to turn (with the _rotateSpeed speed) to the latest direction it was heading even if the movement was stopped. If the new property is turned off, it would behave the same way as it does now. Default is turned on.
- We should add the possibility to add graceTime, meaning that when jumping off a ledge, we could define a time after passing the ledge that player could still perform a jump (by default it is 0).
- Make the crouch mode actually change the physics object to a crouched capsule character and change the mesh to fit that shape.
- Could we add a prop to define a limiter for how much the player can move while in the air (0 = real life so that the player cannot move after jumping or starting to fall, only change direction).
- One bug: When a player jumps on top of a dynamic object (eg. a box) several times in a row, the jump force increases. We should cap the jump force to a constant value.

If for some reason this plan or some of its features can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

Create "Start editor view" plan in docs/plans/p090_start-editor-view.md

Category: Debugger

UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
There should be a debugger "Start view" for the scene view where the engine is not running but the debug camera is still movable and if we change the entity position values, they should change. We currently have the "Runtime view" I am not sure how this should be implemented (could we just have the first frame with the master loop paused? I don't know, study and suggest something.), but the master loop and pause on-screen buttons should be disabled. Design an icon for the "Start view". Changing the view from the "Runtime" view to the "Start" view should only pause the "Runtime"  view and when returned to it, the app should continue where it left of.

This plan should also introduce the select and transform tools (positioned on the center of the left side of the screen). The transform tools should also work in the "Runtime view". These tools are:
- Selection tool [shortcut Ctrl + 1]: Should select the mouse pointer targeted entity in the scene and if double clicked, it should open the edit entity window. When the entity is selected we need to somehow display that it is selected (I would love for it to have an outline, but I would not want to force PostFX on it. If there is way to do it without PostFX and it is not too costly, then do it, otherwise a pulsating wireframe and/or bounding box is fine, or then something else that is user friendly, study the possibilities)
- Transform tool [shortcut Ctrl + 2]: TODO (snapping tools and local/world pos tools should appear)
- Rotation tool [shortcut Ctrl + 3]: TODO (snapping tools and local/world pos tools should appear)
- Scale tool [shortcut Ctrl + 4]: TODO (snapping tools and local/world pos tools should appear)

If for some reason this plan or some of its features can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

Create "Browser default key and mouse behavior mapping and key binding refactoring" plan in docs/plans/p770_browser-default-key-mouse-mapping-and-key-refactoring.md

Category: Shortcuts

UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
We should create a list of the browser's keyboard shortcuts default behaviors are enabled (also consider different browsers). This list in the CONFIG.ts file would look something like this:
{
  defaultBrowserBehavior: {
    F1: true, (options are true, false, or an object { prod: boolean; prodTest: boolean; debug: boolean })
    F5: true,
    CTRL_R: false,
    RIGHT_CLICK_CANVAS: false, (this would disable the right clicking with a mouse on the canvas which acts as it was an image)
    ...
  }
}
Try to map as many of them as you can. If I remember correctly, for example disabling ALT-F4 (on Windows) is not possible and probably some others (maybe), but for apps that build a desktop app (with Electron for example) we could possibly use this CONFIG information to make even those work (not sure).

Also, we should route the default key bindings through the CONFIG.ts file (this can be a following plan). That would mean that each different default key binding list could be opted-out or overwritten in the CONFIG.ts:
{
  runtimeView: {
    ...DEFAULT_RUNTIME_DEBUG_KEY_BINDINGS,
    { overwriteSomeBindingHere }
  },
  materialView: {
    ...DEFAULT_MATERIAL_KEY_BINDINGS,
    { overwriteSomeBindingHere }
  },
  prodTest: {
    DEFAULT_PROD_TEST_KEY_BINDINGS,
    { overwriteSomeBindingHere }
  }
}
This also means that each debug view (runtime or material editor, or in the future some other view) should have their own default key bindings and when a particular view is displayed only that view's key bindings should be enabled and the rest disabled.

We should also refactor the shortcut displaying dialog. We should remove the "U" shortcut (and the "App key shortcuts" button from the Debug tools controls) and just use the "I" shortcut (name the button "Key shortcuts [I]"). When "I" is pressed it opens the dialog and opens the tab that is the current view, and when it is pressed again it should toggle to the next tab. These tabs should be (in this order):
- Runtime (The tab that is now labeled "Ækasha")
- Material Editor (some of the key bindings are the same as Runtime's but they need to be defined again)
- App (current scene) (The same tab that is currently there)
We probably should include the grouping information with the bindings meaning that we should be able to produce each tab's list and grouping with only the key binding array. I don't know how this could be possible but for example add a group binding type (that has all the group information: title, description, orderNr, what else?) with an id and then each actual key binding could get a groupId and they would be listed in that group. This would work the same way for the app key bindings.

In addition to this plan we should create a plan for gathering all of the input bindings from the app/game in the build process (or when starting yarn dev). We should go through the code and gather all app input bindings and what scene they belong to to create a full list of the app's key bindings. We could then create a help/instructions view on the app side with this data (and possibly add the possibility to overwrite these inputs in a game/app). The bindings should have an option to opt-out of being gathered in the build/dev start process.

If for some reason this plan or some of its features can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

************************************

DRAFT_BEER*******************
Add dynamic tier size changing during run time for physics simulation tier sizes.
- Two small engine changes would make runtime changes safe. Each is a fairly small addition:
-- An in-place updatePhysicsTierPolicyRings. It would recompute withinSq / leaveSq on the running policy and keep the pending measurements. Decisions already read the radii when they're made, not when the positions are measured, so the measurements stay valid.
-- An optional per-step transition budget in physicsTierSystem. Applying requests in entity id order would keep it deterministic.
- Longer term, add count caps to the rings (maxMembers per tier, like Mass LOD). That gives you per-area behaviour without authoring zones. Per-area overrides proper belong with p352's Phase 5, cell driving with p353.
